title: Add CSRF/state validation to OAuthBridge
description:
P1 finding from 10-agent swarm codebase audit (P1-013). OAuthBridgeController.ExchangeCode proxies POST body to GitHub with no state validation, no CSRF protection, no content-type restriction. App acts as open OAuth proxy enabling CSRF-based account linking attacks.

File: MemorySmith.App/Controllers/OAuthBridgeController.cs (lines 39-60)
Confidence: 85%
Source: codebase-audit-20260710-agent10-swarm-v2.md

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Audit synthesis corroboration: the redacted audit identifies the anonymous OAuth bridge as an additional hardening concern around callback state, request validation, and default exposure. The state/CSRF portion overlaps this task; residual feature-flag, content-type, and request-size decisions should be handled within this task rather than duplicated.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: 2026-08-08 deep-dive reverified OAuthBridgeController as a separate anonymous transparent proxy: it forwards caller-supplied authorization/token fields without state/PKCE binding, strict allowlisting, content-type/body limits, or a feature gate. Normal GitHub callback handling is more controlled, so this bridge needs independent hardening.
